root_cause.text: The rtl8180 wireless driver’s `rtl8180_init_rx_ring()` error handling failed to clean up partially initialized RX ring state and allocated `skb`/DMA buffers in `priv->rx_buf` when an allocation or DMA mapping error occurred, leaving previously successful per-entry allocations leaked and risking double-free issues on later cleanup.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes direct `dma_free_coherent()` calls from the `rtl8180_init_rx_ring()` failure paths, adds `priv->rx_buf[i] = NULL;` after a DMA mapping failure to prevent double free, and changes `rtl8180_start()` to jump to `err_free_rings`, which calls `rtl8180_free_rx_ring()` to free the partially allocated RX ring.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the RX ring deallocation from the skb allocation failure path in rtl8180_init_rx_ring().
intent_record.what: The error path in rtl8180_init_rx_ring() no longer calls dma_free_coherent() when skb allocation fails; the three-line DMA ring free block was removed, leaving only the error message and -ENOMEM return.
intent_record.how: If RX skb allocation fails during ring initialization, the function now immediately reports the error and exits without freeing the RX ring memory in that branch. The visible effect is a change in cleanup behavior on this failure path, removing deallocation that previously occurred there.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the RX ring initialization error path to clear the failed buffer slot instead of freeing the entire coherent ring buffer.
intent_record.what: In the DMA mapping error path inside rtl8180_init_rx_ring(), the code no longer frees the RX ring coherent DMA buffer directly; instead it sets priv->rx_buf[i] to NULL before logging the error and returning -ENOMEM.
intent_record.how: On an RX skb DMA mapping failure, the driver now leaves the shared RX ring buffer ownership unchanged at this point and clears the per-slot buffer pointer, which avoids prematurely freeing the entire RX ring from this per-entry failure path and marks the failed buffer slot as unused.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix RX ring initialization failure handling to clean up allocated resources before returning an error.
intent_record.what: The error handling after rtl8180_init_rx_ring() changed from an immediate 'return ret;' to 'goto err_free_rings;'.
intent_record.how: On failure to initialize the RX ring, execution now jumps to a cleanup path instead of exiting immediately, allowing previously allocated rings or related resources to be freed before returning the error.

candidates.rationale: This error path frees the entire coherent RX ring buffer when only one skb allocation failed, leaving any previously initialized per-entry skb/DMA state in priv->rx_buf uncleared and causing inconsistent cleanup/leaks.
The function returns immediately after the partial failure without first cleaning up earlier successful RX ring allocations, which is the root cause of leaked resources and later cleanup hazards.
On DMA mapping failure, this statement again deallocates the whole RX ring instead of only rolling back the current slot, which mismatches the partially initialized ring state.

This cleans up only the just-allocated skb on mapping failure, but the subsequent full-ring free skips per-entry cleanup of previously established RX buffer state, contributing to the resource leak/double-free problem.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the full-ring deallocation used on an error path after only a partial RX ring initialization failure. It skips proper rollback of earlier per-entry skb/DMA state in priv->rx_buf, which caused leaked allocations and cleanup inconsistency.

The function exits immediately on allocation failure without first cleaning up the successfully initialized RX ring entries. This leaves partially initialized state behind and is part of the resource leak / later double-free hazard.

On DMA mapping failure, only the newly allocated skb is freed here, while the surrounding error handling still fails to unwind previously allocated RX buffers in priv->rx_buf. That partial cleanup contributed to the inconsistent ring state.
